body.description: Isomorphic, functional type-checking for Javascript. Packaging each test as a function facilitates compact code where a callback is expected.

example.text:
import { isDefined } from 'typical'
const allDefined = array.every(isDefined)

body.description: Returns true if input is a number (including infinity). It is a more reasonable alternative to `typeof n` which returns `number` for `NaN`.

example.text:
> t.isNumber(0)
true
> t.isNumber(1)
true
> t.isNumber(1.1)
true
> t.isNumber(0xff)
true
> t.isNumber(0644)
true
> t.isNumber(6.2e5)
true
> t.isNumber(NaN)
false
> t.isNumber(Infinity)
true

body.params:
Param | Type | Description
---   | ---  | ---
n     | *    | The input to test

body.description: Returns true if input is a finite number. Identical to `isNumber` beside excluding infinity.

example.text:
> t.isFiniteNumber(0)
true
> t.isFiniteNumber(1)
true
> t.isFiniteNumber(1.1)
true
> t.isFiniteNumber(0xff)
true
> t.isFiniteNumber(0644)
true
> t.isFiniteNumber(6.2e5)
true
> t.isFiniteNumber(NaN)
false
> t.isFiniteNumber(Infinity)
false

body.params:

body.description: A plain object is a simple object literal that is not an instance of a class. Returns `true` if the input `typeof` is `object` and is not `null` plus either has a _direct_ prototype of `Object.prototype` or `null`.

example.text:
> t.isPlainObject({ something: 'one' }) // object literal
true
> t.isPlainObject(Object.create(null)) // null-prototype plain object
true
> t.isPlainObject(new Date())
false
> t.isPlainObject([ 0, 1 ])
false
> t.isPlainObject(/test/)
false
> t.isPlainObject(1)
false
> t.isPlainObject('one')
false
> t.isPlainObject(null)
false
> t.isPlainObject((function * () {})())
false
> t.isPlainObject(function * () {})
false

body.params:
Param | Type | Description
---   | ---  | ---
Input | *    | The input to test

body.code:
test.set('.isNumber(value)', function () {
  a.equal(t.isNumber(0), true)
  a.equal(t.isNumber(1), true)
  a.equal(t.isNumber(1.1), true)
  a.equal(t.isNumber(0xff), true)
  a.equal(t.isNumber(6.2e5), true)
  a.equal(t.isNumber(NaN), false)
  a.equal(t.isNumber(Infinity), true)
})

test.set('.isFiniteNumber(value)', function () {
  a.equal(t.isFiniteNumber(0), true)
  a.equal(t.isFiniteNumber(1), true)
  a.equal(t.isFiniteNumber(1.1), true)
  a.equal(t.isFiniteNumber(0xff), true)
  a.equal(t.isFiniteNumber(6.2e5), true)
  a.equal(t.isFiniteNumber(NaN), false)
  a.equal(t.isFiniteNumber(Infinity), false)
})
